sections.text: He who leaves the body with mind unmoved and filled with devotion, by the power of his meditation gathering between his eyebrows his whole vital energy, attains the Supreme.

Now I will speak briefly of the imperishable goal, proclaimed by those versed in the scriptures, which the mystic attains when free from passion, and for which he is content to undergo the vow of continence.
सर्वद्वाराणि संयम्य मनो हृदि निरुध्य च।
Closing the gates of the body, drawing the forces of his mind into the heart and by the power of meditation concentrating his vital energy in the brain;

We had been discussing chapter eight, Akshara Brahma Yoga, Yoga of Imperishable Brahman. And as we have seen so far, the first four verses gave us the nature of the Brahman, the immanence and transcendence of Brahman, that everything they can think about, Shara and Akshara is all Brahman. Its all his manifestation. And then in the next few verses we have seen that how at the time of death, death of the state of existence, death of this thought, death of ego, how one can recognize that permanence of the self. And last few verses, Bhagawan had been giving us the word picture of that imperishable Brahman. So we have seen the Kavim Puranam Anusasitharam that he is omniscient, he is ancient and he is having the lordship over everything.
But that picture also doesnt give us the complete picture. He is minuter than minute. It is not something we can paint a picture in our head or formulate a form in our head. So anything we can formulate a form is not him. It is beyond capacity of our intellect. And Sarvasya Dhaataram Achinte Rupam.
He is a supporter of all and it cannot be thought of. Aditya Varanam tama Sahaprasthat. He is self effulgent. It does not require any other means to know him. By its very nature he reveals himself. Awareness itself is him.
I need to be aware of an object. For an object to be known, I have to be aware of it. So my awareness is necessary to make that object revealed to myself. But my awareness itself does not require anything to be known to me. Awareness itself makes itself available. So the next few verses talked about the Pryanakala.
We have seen the difference between Antakaala and Pryanakala. Priyanakala is the time of departure. I may be coming back. My departure may be for going now and coming back again. Antikala is the last end of it. Im not going anywhere.
Once I go there, Im not coming back. So the one who at the time of departure focus on the nature of the self, he will also achieve that realization of the impermanence. So the whole goal we have seen so far is gaining the experience of something which we have not experienced before. We have been striving all our life -- knowingly or unknowingly.
We have been trying to find a state of existence where there is no sorrow, no imperfection, no unhappiness. That state were constantly struggling to achieve by all the means available to us through our equipment of body, mind, and intellect. We try and employ all three of them to achieve the state of perfection -- where there is no unhappiness, no sorrow, no disease.
And as Bhagavan Buddha found out, there is nothing like that in this world. So there got to be a place or state because otherwise we wont be striving for it. If health is not my nature, I wont be striving for health. Ill be very happy, be unhealthy. But thats not my natural state of my existence. Therefore as soon as something happens, I run to the doctor, fix it.
So unhappiness also cannot be a natural thing to me. However, Im constantly unhappy. So what should I be doing to achieve that? What we have seen last is Yat Aksaram Veda Vido Vadanti -- that imperishable state which the knowers of the Vedas talk about. There is a state where all that you are seeking is available.
Vishyanti Yat Yoho Vit Ragaha. People give up everything in life to achieve that state. Brahmacharyam Charanti. By desiring that people practice Brahmacharya. Last time as we have seen Brahma Acharya Brahmachari. One who is reveling or pursuing the path of Brahman is Brahmachari.
One who is following the path of action is a Karmachari. In Hindi, as we have discussed last time, the clerks are called Karmacharis. But you know, one who is their boss is called Adyaksha. One who keeps eye on them is Adyaksha. So we are Karmachari in all our day to day life. Because we constantly see what is next.
I have done this, Ive been there. Somebody says, Take a cruise -- I have done it. Tell me something else which I can do. Because we are constantly asking, what is next, what will be our next action? Brahmacharya is constantly seeking how to become one with Brahman -- that is a Brahmachari. And who is the Adyaksha?
In this case, our consciousness is keeping an eye on whats happening. Tatte padam sangrahena pravakshye -- Im going to tell you about that state of existence which you have been seeking all your life, which you have tried everything to achieve so far but have not attained. Im going to tell you in a summary.
Now Bhagavan explains how that state can be achieved. So the next verse says sarvadvarani samyamya mano ruddin irudhyyacha murdni adhay atmanah pranam astito yogadharana. This is obviously explaining the technique of meditation. We want to experience that state. I cannot be experiencing in our day to day life, but at least I can have a glimpse in my meditation. In meditation what I get is a glimpse of that state where there is no unhappiness, there is no sorrow.
But that cannot be just 20 minutes a day or 30 minutes a day, once in the morning and once in the evening. It has to be a continuous state of existence. I am not seeking temporary happiness; Im seeking permanent happiness. It says Sarva dwarani samyamya. So far, everything that has caused me unhappiness is because of my sense perception. When I see that the temperature outside is not conducive to my liking, because I feel it, then I feel unhappy.
So senses are telling me whether its conducive or not. If that information is not available to me, then I will not know. Just as in my deep sleep, Im not aware what temperature the room is, whether Donald Trump is winning or Hillary Clinton is ahead. None of that exists in my deep sleep. So the first thing we notice is that these senses are causing agitation in my mind. Sarva dwarani samyamya -- lets experience what happens when I close all the gates of information.
You know, people who take retreats these days -- its very difficult to take a true retreat. Ten or twenty years ago when we used to take retreats, they would say, you cant take a radio with you, you cannot take anything with you. Dont listen to radio, dont listen to television. But now people take their phone -- and everything, television included, is on your phone. The idea of a retreat was that you are constantly bombarded with information which distracts you, so at least for that week,
You are cut off from the world outside. Whats happening politically, whats happening in a profession, all that youre not listening. So this takes that idea to an extreme and say close all your senses when you sit down in meditation. Sarva dwarani Samyami. Controlling all your gates. Manohrudi Nirudhyacha.
Placing your mind in your heart. In a sense, placing your mind -- which was running outside in day-to-day life -- inward. The minds job is to go outside and get information, like the clerk who is gathering all the data from outside and reporting it to the intellect, the adyaksha, to decipher the data. Now, make that mind turn inward.
Hriddi means inward -- basically, focus on yourself. Your thoughts should be one and one alone: What is my real self? Thats the thought, one single thought. Murdni Adhaya Atmanah -- having your pranas in your head. Now this looks like very high-level yogic exercise.
Now it can be but you can look at it in many different ways. At our level, this is a technique of a meditation when at least for those 20 minutes youre trying to cut off yourself from this world. You cut off yourself from your senses, cut off all your mind from running out and turn inward. Then say Murdni a day atman. Focus all your pranas into your head. Now sit down for meditation.
See where you feel any life. At that time, all your focus will be on your head. Therefore in the technical meditation chapter six we said focus your mind between your two eyebrows. Because youre not aware of rest of the body, youre dropping all your awareness about the rest of your body. Youre focusing only the one thing, one thing alone. Your computer which is functioning at that time in your head.
They said, placing your pranas -- all the physiological activities happening in your body -- youre only aware of whats happening in your mind, at the head, at that time. Therefore pranayama helps, because first you focus on the breathing. Right now Im focusing on everything that is happening in my body: my legs are moving, my hands are moving, my lips are moving. When doing meditation you stop thinking about your legs and hands and mouth and you only start thinking about whats happening in your mind. So when you first start focusing only on your breath, you are not focusing on anything else which is going on in your body. That puts you in a state where mind will calm down. And then you can just focus on who I am.
So only one thought and one thought alone. Pranam astitha Yogadharanam. One who has been practicing this over and over and over again can achieve the state of meditation very easily. And the next verse says Omiti ek aksaram Brahma -- this is truly a technique of meditation we have learned in chapter six. Hes putting it again in a very succinct manner for you to understand.
What is the goal of meditation? The goal of meditation is to give us a glimpse of that state where there is no limitation, no unhappiness, no sorrow -- just bliss. So once you have now controlled your senses and your mind and your pranas: Omiti ek aksaram Brahma vyaharan mam anusmaran -- chant the one syllable Om, which is the sound symbol of God. God can be pictured in many different ways, but the simplest and most non-distracting form is the word Om. And we have seen before --
The Om represents the creation, sustenance and destruction or the past, present and future. But that one word contains everything that needs to be known about the self. So Vyaharan Mam Anusmaran -- while uttering that one syllable Om, remember Me. Dont just get focused on the sound alone. Im thinking about that self which is all-pervading, and the Om is representing it.
First you can start chanting out loud, then gradually lower your pitch, and then just chant in your mind -- constantly thinking about that one self and that one self alone, which pervades everywhere -- while chanting Aum. Yah prayati tyajan Deham -- one who leaves this body, you can consider that as your death. That is the time of death. All this which we have learned in these last two verses, we all have known. Looking at people who have died in front of your eyes, it is not possible to meditate at the time of death. You are not there to meditate.
You have no control over whats happening. So this verse is actually about the death in your meditation -- the death of your identification with your body, mind and intellect. Yaha prayati tyajan Deham. The complete detachment from the identification with this body. In my meditation Sa yati paramam gatima he experiences that supreme state of existence.
If you perfect your meditation to a point that I can Control all my senses.

These verses reveal a practical meditation technique: Sarva dvarani samyamya, close all the gates of the senses; Mano hridi nirudhya, draw the mind inward to the heart; Murdhni adhaya atmanah pranam, focus the vital energy in the head. This is not esoteric instruction reserved for advanced yogis, it describes what happens naturally when we truly withdraw attention from external stimulation. Consider how retreats work: by removing radio, television, and now phones, we close the gates of information that constantly agitate the mind. This week, create a mini-retreat for yourself. Set aside 20 minutes where you consciously close all gates, no phone, no conversation, no reading. Notice how when external input stops, awareness naturally turns inward and begins to settle in the heart, the center of your being.
The teaching about focusing pranas in the head during meditation has a practical interpretation for daily practice. When you sit for meditation, begin by noticing where you feel alive in your body, this is prana. Through breath awareness, gradually let go of awareness of your limbs, your torso, and gather your sense of aliveness into your head, particularly between your eyebrows. This is not about straining; it is about selective attention. Just as you can choose to feel the sensation in your left thumb right now, you can choose to center your awareness. The goal, as verse 11 states, is to glimpse that imperishable state which the knowers of the Vedas speak of, a state without limitation, without sorrow, of pure bliss. Your 20-minute meditation becomes a dress rehearsal for the ultimate letting go. What are you practicing? What are you becoming skilled at releasing?
